slides.heading: Search In Sorted Matrix
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Searching
slides.narration: Let's solve Search In Sorted Matrix, a medium searching problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Rows and columns are sorted ascending; return [row, col] of target or [-1, -1].
Start top-right and eliminate a row or column each step.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Rows and columns are sorted ascending; return row, col of target or -1, -1 . Start top-right and eliminate a row or column each step.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Start at the top-right: moving left decreases, moving down increases, so each step eliminates a row or column.
slides.narration: Start at the top-right: moving left decreases, moving down increases, so each step eliminates a row or column.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Binary search each row → O(r log c)
Start top-right, eliminate a row or column per step → O(r + c)
slides.narration: Scanning everything ignores the sorting. Binary-searching each row is better. Starting at the top-right corner, every comparison eliminates a whole row or column, so it's r plus c.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 4. Return the coordinates or minus ones
slides.narration: Step by step. First, start top-right. Second, if too big, move left. Third, if too small, move down. Fourth, return the coordinates or minus ones.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.narration: At 1000: too big, so everything below is too, move left.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.narration: At 15: too small, so everything left is too, move down.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.narration: At 32: too small, so everything left is too, move down.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.narration: At 35: too small, so everything left is too, move down.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.narration: At 45: too big, so everything below is too, move left.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We start at row zero and the last column. While in bounds, return on a match, move left if the value is too big, otherwise move down.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n plus m. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Top-right or bottom-left both work, because one move increases and the other decreases. From top-left both increase, so you can't decide.
